Chapter Seven: Managing Time—Prioritization and the Art of Saying No
You know, time really is our most precious resource. No matter how organized we are, there’s only so much of it in a day. So, managing time isn’t just about filling up a calendar—it's about making smart choices about what truly deserves our attention, and just as importantly, what we need to let go of.
Prioritization? It’s the secret sauce. It means figuring out the difference between what’s screaming for your attention right now, and what’s actually going to move the needle in the long run.
It’s so easy to fall into the trap of checking off a bunch of tiny, low-impact tasks just because it feels good to be busy. But are those tasks really helping you reach your biggest goals? That’s the question we need to ask ourselves regularly.
One simple, powerful tool you can use is the Eisenhower Matrix. Imagine four boxes:
First, there are tasks that are urgent and important. Handle those right away.
Next, important but not urgent—these are the projects that push you forward over time, so make sure to actually schedule them.
Then, there are urgent but not important things. These are the classic distractions—can you hand them off, or at least spend less time on them?
And finally, the things that are neither urgent nor important. Honestly, just let those go. Free up your energy for what really matters.
Let’s bring this to life. Picture a nonprofit director who’s constantly juggling fundraising, managing her team, and handling community events. She maps all her tasks onto the matrix, and suddenly it’s clear: she’s been spending way too much time replying to endless emails—urgent, but not important—while strategic planning, which is crucial for her mission, keeps getting pushed aside. By shifting her focus, she’s able to carve out time for the work that truly makes a difference.
And then there’s the art of saying no. It’s tough, right? Especially when requests come from people you care about or want to impress. But if you’re always saying yes, your calendar fills up with everyone else’s priorities instead of your own. The trick is to say no kindly, maybe by explaining your current commitments or connecting it back to the bigger picture everyone’s working toward. That way, you’re still protecting your time without burning bridges.
Here are a few simple ways to stay on top of your time:
Start every morning by checking in on your top priorities. What’s the one thing you need to accomplish today?
Try batching similar tasks together—like answering all your emails in one go or setting aside time just for meetings. It cuts down on switching gears and helps you stay focused.
And don’t forget to build in breaks. Short pauses throughout the day can keep your energy up and help you avoid burnout.
At the end of the day, managing time well is about making choices that line up with your values and your biggest dreams. When you focus on what truly matters and learn to say no with confidence, you open up space—not just for work, but for your own well-being and growth.
